links.comparator_used: Same questions answered by the same chatbots with the default prompt, with no reading-level instruction
links.outcome: Reading level of chatbot responses (Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level) relative to the reader's question level
links.effect: Default: every chatbot answered above the question's level (median difference +1.21 to +3.57 grades). With a sixth-grade instruction, the median gap narrowed in every model and 3 of 5 models answered below the reader's level (100 questions, 1,500 responses).
links.quote: Given an explicit sixth-grade instruction, the median gap narrowed in every model and three of five answered below the reader's level.

links.comparator_used: Default chatbot output with no instruction to match the reader's level (fixed output regardless of the asker)
links.outcome: Whether chatbot reading level adapted to the reader's level (FKGL gap between response and question)
links.effect: Without instruction, every chatbot answered above the question's level (median +1.21 to +3.57 grades). With an instruction to match the reader's level or answer at sixth-grade level, the gap narrowed in every model.
links.quote: Chatbots do not adapt to the reader by default, but can when instructed.
